B.1.5 CAPEX considerations Captial expenditures (CAPEX) associated with standing up a fully functional machine shop to produce welded linacs at a rate of 2 per month in full production would be significant, but not unreasonable. Even if we assume that each quadrant will take 40 hours of machine time, the most complex highest value piece parts in the linac could easily be completed with one dedicated machine and two shift operation. Another dedicated machine would be required in order to perform post weld machining operations although even with an allowance of 80 hours of machine time for all post weld operations, a single shift month is sufficient. The machine tool cost for the required class of machine would be on the order of $0.5M-$1M with an additional: $1M for multiple lower grade machine tools to manufacture less precise ancillary components; $1M for high precision coordinate measuring machines; $1M for facilities improvements such as floor space demising, equipment foundation rigidization, climate control and material handling; $0.25M for ancillary expenses such as CAD/CAM, basic support equipment including saws, grinders, manual inspection tools; $0.1M per machine for basic infrastructure (compressed air, coolant handling, electrical, office equipment). Of the course the above assumes an existing suitable facility floor space of approximately 8-10k sq. ft. The above considerations apply onto to piece part fabrication and additional space would be required for chemical cleaning, an EBW or two and final RF cold and hot testing. It is also prudent to mention that equipment downtime can significantly effect production schedules and thus some degree of redundancy would be recommended, with schedule risk tolerance being the determining factor when considering the amount of redundancy required. The above would place a total in the range of $6-8M of CAPEX to stand up a greenfield machine shop capable of handling the ~2 linac/month rate once in production. If developed as an ‘add-on’ to an existing firm’s machine shop, significant savings could be realized with the above number reduced at least in half to $2-4M. This figure does not account for running expenses to cover lease, power, maintenance and repair. B.1.6 Personnel considerations Of course personnel are critical to successful machine shop deployment. Fortunately, precision machine shop staff are still available in the domestic workforce although wage requirements have been growing significantly over the decades. Having said that, there is still specialized handling and process familiarization ramp up time required and some of the beachhead staff would need to be recruited from existing linac manufacturers or national laboratories. An estimate of 25+ personnel would be required to permit 2 shift operation of such a facility.
